previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for dizziness, worsening headache, and melena with a significant drop in hemoglobin from 37.5 to 25.5. Evaluation revealed guaiac-positive stool and a history of chronic GVHD, long-term steroid use, and anticoagulation with enoxaparin. CT head showed no acute intracranial process. EGD revealed duodenal erosions with recent bleeding, and colonoscopy showed a sigmoid ulcer and diverticulosis. Capsule endoscopy did not identify an active bleed. H. pylori infection was confirmed, and treatment with amoxicillin and clarithromycin was initiated. Enoxaparin was held during acute bleeding and restarted at a reduced dose of 40 mg daily prior to discharge. Hemoglobin improved to 10.5, and the patient was discharged home with plans for follow-up on pending biopsies, sirolimus level, and platelet function studies.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___

COMPARISON:  Prior chest CT from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Weakness, question pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest are provided demonstrating
resolution  of bilateral subtle ground-glass and nodular opacities.  No large
effusion or pneumothorax is seen.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.
Bony structures are intact.  Clips in the upper abdomen noted.

IMPRESSION:  Significant interval improvement in aeration of the lungs with no
residual consolidation seen.

HISTORY:  Patient with acute on chronic low back pain.

TECHNIQUE:  T1-T2 and inversion recovery sagittal and T2 axial images of the
lumbar spine.

COMPARISON:  Comparison was made with a prior abdominal CT of ___.

FINDINGS:

From T11 -12 to L5-S1 level, mild disk degenerative change and mild bulging
seen without spinal stenosis or foraminal narrowing.  No evidence of nerve
root displacement.

The superior endplate of L5 vertebra demonstrates mild compression with low T1
and slightly high convexity complex signal indicating of subacute to chronic
compression.  This finding was present on the previous abdominal CT.  There is
no acute compression fracture seen.

The distal spinal cord.  Paraspinal soft tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Mild degenerative changes are seen in the lumbar region without spinal
stenosis or nerve root displacement.  Subacute to chronic compression of the
superior endplate of L5 vertebra identified as unchanged from previous
abdominal CT of ___.

TYPE OF THE EXAM:  CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis.

REASON FOR THE EXAM AND MEDICAL HISTORY:  History of CML presenting with
band-like pain, evaluate for fracture, pulmonary process suggestive of drug
toxicity.

TECHNIQUE:

Multiple axial CT images through the chest, abdomen and pelvis were obtained
post-administration of intravenous contrast and ingestion of oral contrast.

Coronal and sagittal reconstructions are obtained.

COMPARISON EXAMS:  ___ and CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis.

FINDINGS:

CHEST:  Thyroid gland is normal in appearance.  There is no axillary,
supraclavicular, or mediastinal lymphadenopathy.  Heart is normal size.  There
is no pericardial effusion.  There are coronary artery calcifications and
calcified hilar lymph nodes probably likely secondary to prior granulomatous
disease.

Evaluation of the lung parenchyma demonstrates a right upper lobe granuloma as
well as residual patchy airspace ground-glass opacities which are less
extensive compared to the prior study.  There is no pleural effusion.

ABDOMEN:  Liver enhances homogeneously without evidence of focal masses. 
Patient is status post cholecystectomy.  Spleen is not enlarged.  Bilateral
adrenal glands and bilateral kidneys are unremarkable.  There is again seen a
cystic lesion within the pancreatic head, measuring 1.7 x 1.1 cm (2:60). 
There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation.  The remaining
pancreas is slightly atrophic, however, unremarkable.

There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.  The oral contrast
has transited throughout the small loops of bowels, which are not dilated or
demonstrate any wall abnormality.

PELVIS:

Uterus is normal in appearance.  Urinary bladder is well distended without
evidence of focal masses.  There is gas distention of the sigmoid colon
without evidence of abnormal wall thickening or proximal obstruction.  There
is no lymphadenopathy or free fluid within the pelvis.

VASCULAR STRUCTURES:  There is no evidence to significant atherosclerotic
disease, aneurysmal dilatation.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There is again seen a compression fracture of L5
vertebral body with endplate sclerosis, unchanged compared to the prior study.
T11 vertebral body, appears to have increasing sclerosis with relatively
stable loss of anterior body height. 

IMPRESSION:

1. Resolving bilateral patchy airspace opacities with residual scattered
minimal bilateral airspace opacity in the lungs.  No evidence of
lymphadenopathy within the chest, abdomen or pelvis.

2. Stable appearance of L5 compression fracture with increasing end plate
sclerosis of T11 and relatively stable loss of anterior verterbal body height,
indicating compression fracture. 

3. Stable size of pancreatic head cystic lesion, for which baseline MRCP is
recommended.

HISTORY:  ___ woman, with loss of height of T11; assess for acute
fracture.

COMPARISON:  CT chest, abdomen and pelvis on ___.  Also limited
comparison from MR lumbar spine on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar, multisequence T1- and T2-weighted images were
acquired through the thoracic spine, without IV contrast administration.

FINDINGS:  There is wedge deformity of the T11 vertebral body, with
approximately 25% of loss of height, anteriorly.  On the "water" IDEAL
sequence, there is diffuse but band-like hyperintensity involving
predominately the superior portion of the vertebral body.  The findings are
compatible with acute compression fracture. There is no evidence of extension
of bone edema to the posterior elements, and no retropulsion of its dorsal
cortex, canal compromise or effacement of the thecal sac.  The subjacent
portion of the spinal cord demonstrates no signal abnormality to suggest cord
contusion.  There is mild prevertebral fluid hyperintensity at T11. The dorsal
paraspinal soft tissues are unremarkable. 

There is no overall spinal malalignment. At T6-T7, a large (4.5 mm) right
paracentral disc protrusion indents the ventral spinal cord (6:8), and at
T7-T8, a left paracentral protrusion likely impinges upon the exiting left T7
nerve root (3:8, 6:13).  The remainder of the thoracic spinal canal remains
capacious.  Minimal degenerative changes are noted with minor endplate
irregularity at the T6-T7 and T12-L1 levels. 

The thoracic spinal cord remains normal in signal intensity and morphology.  

IMPRESSION:  
1.  Acute-to-subacute T11 anterior wedge compression fracture, without
retropulsion into the canal.  
2.  No evidence of spinal cord signal abnormality to suggest cord injury.  
3.  No thoracic spinal malalignment.
4.  T6-T7 and T7-8: Relatively large right and left paracentral disc
herniations, respectively, indent the spinal cord and impinge upon the exiting
nerve roots.

HISTORY:  New pancreatic mass.  Evaluate biliary tree.  

COMPARISON:  CT dated ___. 

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1 and T2 weighted images were acquired on a 1.5 Tesla
magnet obtained prior to, during and after the uneventful intravenous
administration of 7 mL of Gadavist.  The patient also received 2.5 mL of
Gadavist diluted with 75 mL of water p.o..  

A non-breath hold protocol had to be performed as the patient could not hold
her breath.  

FINDINGS:

There are multiple cystic lesions within the pancreas, with the largest
measuring 1.8 cm within the head of the pancreas (6:1).  There is no definite
communication between the cystic lesions and the main pancreatic duct.  The
main pancreatic duct is of normal caliber.  The pancreas is otherwise atrophic
and there is lipomatous replacement of pancreatic parenchyma. 

The biliary tree is normal.  The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  No
filling defects in the biliary tree. 

The liver is within normal limits.  No focal liver lesions.  The portal and
hepatic veins are patent.  Note is made of a surgical clip adjacent to the
posterior aspect of the right lobe of the liver (16:13). 

The kidneys and adrenals are within normal limits.  The spleen is
unremarkable.  The visualized small and large bowel is unremarkable.  No
retroperitoneal or mesenteric adenopathy.  The lung bases are clear. 

There is an anterior wedge compression fracture at T11 with bone marrow edema
identified within this vertebral body, consistent with an acute/subacute
fracture.  There is also a chronic anterior wedge compression fracture of L5. 
There is approximately 25% loss of vertebral body height at both levels.  No
destructive osseous lesions.  

 IMPRESSION:

1.  Multiple cystic lesions in the pancreas, largest measuring 1.8 cm in the
head of the pancreas.  Statistically these most likely represent side branch
IPMNs.  Follow-up MRI in 6 months is recommended. 

2. Normal biliary tree. 

3.  Anterior wedge compression fractures at T11 and L5 with <25% loss of
vertebral body height. Edema at fracture site at T11 suggestive of
acute/subacute fracture. L5 compression fracture appears chronic.

HISTORY:  Increased abdominal pain, evaluate for abdominal pathology.

COMPARISON:  CT torso from ___, MRCP from ___ and abdominal
radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:

Two frontal images of the abdomen demonstrate a nonspecific bowel gas pattern.
There are a few air-fluid levels in the right lower quadrant; however, air is
seen within the colon to the rectum.  No dilated loops of small bowel are
appreciated.  No free intraperitoneal air is identified.

IMPRESSION:

Nonspecific bowel gas pattern with no free air.
